title: Carrots, canned, cooked with butter or margarine

content.title: About
content.content: Canned carrots cooked with butter or margarine are sliced carrot pieces that have been boiled until tender and then sealed in a jar with added butter or margarine. The product is ready to eat and is often used as a side dish or ingredient in salads and other recipes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Canned carrots retain most of the vitamin A derived from beta‑carotene.
The added fat improves absorption of fat‑soluble vitamins.
Properly stored, the jars can last 2‑3 years.
These conserves have traditionally been made in colder climates where fresh vegetables are scarce in winter.
Margarine is frequently used as a more affordable alternative to butter.

items.title: Rich in beta‑carotene
items.content: Beta‑carotene is converted in the body to vitamin A, which supports vision, immunity, and skin health.

items.title: Supports cardiovascular health
items.content: The plant fiber and potassium help maintain normal blood pressure.

items.title: Source of antioxidants
items.content: In addition to beta‑carotene, carrots provide vitamin C and flavonoids that combat free radicals.

items.title: Aids digestion
items.content: Fiber promotes regular bowel movements and a healthy gut microbiome.

items.title: Improves vitamin absorption
items.content: Fats from butter or margarine enhance the uptake of fat‑soluble vitamins A, D, E, and K.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Canned products are often salted; people with hypertension should monitor intake.

items.title: Dairy allergy risk
items.content: If butter is used, individuals allergic to dairy may react.

items.title: Possible trans fats
items.content: Some margarines contain trans fats, which are detrimental to heart health.

items.title: Preservative considerations
items.content: Certain batches may include additives such as sulfites; those sensitive should be cautious.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Canned carrots can be eaten straight from the jar, added to salads, used as a cold appetizer, served as a side with meat or fish, or incorporated into casseroles and soups.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the unopened jar in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. After opening, keep it refrigerated in a sealed container and consume within 3‑5 days. Discard if the jar bulges, develops an off‑odor, or shows discoloration.
